raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I cannot take big risks. I do what has worked on my land and what people around me do. Wheat and maize together keep the land busy and give steadier grain. I cannot spend too much at once because the family still needs cash for daily life, and some people work outside, so field work must be done on time and simply. I have well water, so if it turns dry I can save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not water more than needed.

For wheat, I will still sow in early October, same as usual in our place. I will use the common local improved seed people nearby buy, not anything fancy. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then watch the wheat color after winter. If the leaves look pale when it starts growing strongly, I will add another bit of nitrogen. Wheat is important, so I would rather not let it go hungry. I will water around before winter, then at jointing, and again at filling if spring is dry. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant maize right away. That turnaround is always tight, so I will do light rotary tillage or direct planting after harvest if I can get it done quickly. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most families here. I will not over-spend on fertilizer, but I will still give enough base fertilizer and one topdress when the maize gets taller. If summer rain is normal, one irrigation may be enough; if it rains well, maybe none. I spray only if I really see weeds or insects, because medicine also costs money.
